questions.question: You need to distinguish “electrophilic addition” from several related chapter concepts. Which description uniquely identifies it?

options.label: A
options.text: The principle stating that the structure of a transition state resembles the species (reactant or intermediate/product) to which it is closest in free energy.

options.label: B
options.text: The progressive thermodynamic stabilization of carbocations with increasing alkyl substitution: tertiary (3°) > secondary (2°) > primary (1°) > methyl.

options.label: C
options.text: The empirical rule stating that electrophilic addition of HX to an unsymmetrical alkene attaches the hydrogen to the less substituted carbon, forming the more stable carbocation.

options.label: D
options.text: A fundamental reaction of alkenes where an electrophile attacks the electron-rich pi bond, generating a carbocation intermediate before nucleophilic capture.

questions.correct_answer: A fundamental reaction of alkenes where an electrophile attacks the electron-rich pi bond, generating a carbocation intermediate before nucleophilic capture.
